what_the_first_dry_run_would_have_shippe.finding: The allocator optimised bytes under a BPW budget and did NOT treat beating the constant-mean null as a constraint. 18 of 859 activation-aware tensors fell BELOW their null -- carrying 17 percent of the activation-aware weight mass.
what_the_first_dry_run_would_have_shippe.why_it_would_have_been_another_collapse: A tensor below its constant-mean null carries no information -- it is worse than emitting the mean row. An lm_head below its null produces logits worse than the mean, which is exactly Math-Preserve's failure mode. The campaign already learned this the expensive way: General-R0 needed lm_head and embed_tokens natively protected, and this allocation was compressing them below null again.
what_the_first_dry_run_would_have_shippe.caught_by: reading the dry-run's own per-tensor beats_null field rather than its headline BPW

the_fix.change: beating the null is now a HARD CONSTRAINT in the allocator, not a scoring term. The lowest rank chosen is the lowest rank that BEATS its null; a tensor that cannot beat its null at any available rank falls through to native pass-through.
the_fix.billing: native is billed at source width, derived from n_weights, because an activation-aware measurement carries no pass_through_bytes field. Getting that wrong would have under-billed the very tensors being protected.

measured_cost_of_the_constraint.why_that_figure_is_misleading: The pilot window is 4 of 78 layers and happens to contain BOTH global tensors. lm_head and embed_tokens are 14.2 percent of the WINDOW but only 0.253 percent of the MODEL, and they do not recur -- every other layer is experts and attention.

whole_model_projection.for_comparison: Math-Preserve, semantically collapsed, shipped 92.0 GB at 0.9774 BPW

measured_cost_of_the_constraint.reading: Protecting the two global tensors natively costs about 0.04 BPW whole-model. It is close to free at model scale and it removes the single most likely cause of another collapse.

what_is_still_unproven: that a pack built this way generates. Per-tensor beats-null is necessary, not sufficient, and no whole-model gate is measurable on a 4-of-78-layer window.
the 0.091 BPW projection assumes recurring layers behave like the pilot's. It is a projection from 1.78 percent of the model's weights.
down_proj is scored against a Gaussian intermediate probe because the capsules hold no intermediate activations. up and gate use real pre_router_hidden.
next: run the full program -- measurement shardwise streaming, allocation global, packing shardwise -- then run tools/condense/glm52_capability_gate.py against the result BEFORE anything trains on it. Projected ~4.9 hours by the packer's own timing model.
